subject: civics
question_text: In what ways is a hawker different from a shop owner?
answer_text:
Hawker: (i) Do not have permanent shops. (ii) Generally sells non branded items, fruits, vegetables, cutlery etc. (iii) Don't have expenses like electricity bills, rents, workers etc. (iv) Sells cheaper as well as costlier products.
Shop Owner: (i) Have permanent shops. (ii) Sells branded as well as non branded items. (iii) Have expenses like electricity bills, rents, workers etc. (iv) Sells products at cheaper rate.
final_answer: Hawkers and shop owners differ in terms of permanence, types of goods sold, expenses, and pricing.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of market structures and differences.

subject: civics
question_text: Compare and contrast a weekly market and a shopping complex on the following: Market, Kind of goods sold, Prices of goods, Sellers, Buyers.
answer_text:
Weekly Market: Non branded, cheaper goods, sold by locals, targeted at low income buyers.
Shopping Complex: Branded, good quality, costlier goods, sold by companies, targeted at high income buyers.
final_answer: Weekly markets cater to local, low-income buyers with non-branded goods, while shopping complexes serve high-income buyers with branded products.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves comparison and understanding of different market types.

subject: civics
question_text: Explain how a chain of markets is formed. What purpose does it serve?
answer_text: A chain of markets is formed as products pass from one market to another. It serves the purpose of allowing consumers to buy goods from far-off places, helps factories and producers reach consumers, encourages production, and provides employment opportunities.
final_answer: The chain of markets facilitates the distribution of goods and creates economic opportunities.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of market dynamics and economic principles.

subject: civics
question_text: 'All persons have equal rights to visit any shop in a marketplace.' Do you think this is true of shops with expensive products? Explain with examples.
answer_text: While all persons have equal rights to visit any shop, this is not always true for shops with expensive products. For example, big commercial shops may not allow poor people to enter, considering them inferior. Additionally, people from lower income groups may hesitate to enter such shops as they cannot afford branded products.
final_answer: Thus, economic barriers can restrict access to shops with expensive products.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves social and economic analysis of market access.

subject: civics
question_text: 'Buying and selling can take place without going to a marketplace.' Explain this statement with the help of examples.
answer_text: Buying and selling can occur without visiting a marketplace through e-commerce companies that provide home delivery. People can order products online or via phone, and payment can be made through plastic money and internet banking.
final_answer: Therefore, modern technology allows for transactions without physical market visits.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of e-commerce and modern payment methods.
